transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-19
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marta (Greenshore Head of Platform), Evan (ML Eng), Samir (Security)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to map Greenshore's developer-led trial -> pilot path. Focus on time to first token, credits, and security constraints.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. priya's our solutions engineer, she'll do the tech bits. 
[00:12] Marta: thanks Jordan. We're trying to figure out how fast we can get a tiny pilot running — some self-serve devs want to ship an assistant in prod like, uh, later this quarter.
[00:22] Priya: great. quick Q first, is the team leaning towards self-serve hosted API or do you anticipate needing a dedicated pool or VPC from day one?
[00:30] Evan: good question. for the first sprint we want self-serve to move fast — free credits and SDKs — but our security team flagged potential residency and KMS needs that might push us to dedicated or VPC for pilot.
[00:42] Samir: yea i'll pause you there. we're regulated — financial services — so keys must be customer-managed, and audit logs need retention for 7 years. also SOC 2 plus ISO-27k, ideally.
[00:55] Jordan: totally reasonable. we have Hosted for rapid PLG onramp with free credits and the same API surface. Dedicated gives reserved capacity and isolated GPU pools. Private/VPC/on-prem is available for strict KMS/HSM locks and network isolation.
[01:10] Marta: can you give a realistic time-to-first-token if we go self-serve? devs expect TTFT in hours not days.
[01:18] Priya: yes — for a typical quickstart using our SDK and example repo, TTFT is often in under 2 hours — often minutes — assuming user can run a sample request. We'll provision the free credits, add a quickstart workspace, and you get console + SDK access. The bottlenecks are onboarding SSO and internal approvals if Samir's team needs to review.
[01:35] Evan: two hours sounds perfect. what's the caveat with latency? the app is interactive, sub-300ms per token is prefered.
[01:44] Priya: so latency depends on model choice and hosting. Hosted with our optimized small-medium models — we call them rdb-7b-lite internally — you can get 150-250ms per token for short context. For strict sub-200 consistently you'd typically pick Dedicated with pinned instances and shorter batch windows. There's also quantization and kernel selection that matter.
[02:05] Jordan: oh quick note — sorry if i garbled product names in the doc earlier, the catalog has the performance profiles by model. we'll send the benchmark spreadsheet after.
[02:14] Samir: you mentioned audit logs retention. do hosted plans provide customer-level audit exports, or is that enterprise-only?
[02:22] Priya: Hosted has audit logs and request traces exposed in the console; for 7-year retention that's typically an enterprise add-on or Dedicated/Private, where we can integrate with your S3/GCS archive or a SIEM. We can bundle extended log retention as an add-on.
[02:38] Marta: and SSO? we use Okta and SAML.
[02:42] Jordan: SSO/SAML supported across all modes; we integrate with Okta for RBAC. For private deployments we can do SAML + SCIM sync more tightly.
[02:51] Evan: what's the expected effort to move from self-serve hosted pilot to Dedicated? we want minimal app changes.
[02:59] Priya: that's a big Redwood differentiator — the same API surface. you can pin model versions and change routing to dedicated nodes without code changes. there will be infra config changes and a migration plan, but client code remains the same. we do canary rollouts and A/B model routing.
[03:18] Samir: curious about KV cache — can we pre-warm or have prefix caching? we use a lot of short-context prompts and want to avoid repeated cost.
[03:26] Priya: yes, our runtime supports prefix/KV cache and automated caching suggestions from Redwood Optimize. For high-throughput we recommend persistent KV cache for short repeated context, that reduces tokens and cost.
[03:36] Marta: ok, credits — how many and for how long?
[03:40] Jordan: we usually provision an initial pool for PLG pilots — i'm proposing 50k free credits for Greenshore to run dev sprints and a benchmark. they typically last 30–60 days depending on usage but we can extend.
[03:52] Evan: can you do a benchmark against our latency SLO? we can schedule a test run from our eu-west infra.
[03:58] Priya: yes — we can run a scheduled benchmark. Two paths: first, a hosted benchmark from our nearest region; second, if you need more realistic throughput we can run a dedicated benchmark using reserved nodes or a private deployment in your VPC. That second requires more setup.
[04:15] Jordan: also note that model quantization choices affect throughput. 4-bit quantization on some open models will cut cost but may increase small hallucination risk — we'd recommend testing on your eval prompts.
[04:28] Evan: on hallucinations — we have regression tests. can we wire Redwood evals to our CI?
[04:34] Priya: yeah, Redwood Optimize supports eval hooks and quality monitoring; you can push prompt sets and metrics to trigger regression alerts. We also have SDKs for automated eval runs in CI.
[04:48] Samir: security again — KMS. you said customer-managed keys are possible with private/VPC; can hosted also integrate with external KMS?
[04:58] Priya: Hosted supports envelope encryption and we can integrate with a customer's KMS via cross-account roles in certain enterprise arrangements, but full HSM-backed key control is typically with Private or Dedicated + VPC where your key material never leaves your account. We'll send details.
[05:14] Marta: any gotchas for compliance? we need SOC2 type II, ISO, and we may have to show crypto certs.
[05:21] Jordan: we have a security pack — SOC2 attestation, pen test summary, ISO intake. We'll attach the security packet. For audits we can provide logs and access reports.
[05:30] Evan: ok great. timeline? if devs start tomorrow, and we accept the free credits, when can we have a running app?
[05:36] Priya: realistically: day 0 — grant credits and create the org; day 1 — devs pull SDK and run simple generate; within 48 hours if nothing blocks with SSO or approvals you can be hitting first tokens and instrumenting evals.
[05:49] Marta: there's also legal — can we do a standard DPA?
[05:53] Jordan: yes, we have a standard DPA and security addenda. Legal can sign the DPA for the pilot; enterprise contract is separate.
[05:59] Samir: for the benchmark — we need to see per-route token cost and token-level latency graphs.
[06:06] Priya: our Console provides token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency. We'll run the benchmark and share graphs; if you want raw traces we can export them.
[06:15] Evan: great. also curious about vector DB integrations; we use Weaviate for embeddings and retrieval.
[06:20] Priya: we have first-class embeddings and you can push vectors to Weaviate, Pinecone, or our internal caching layer. People use hybrid retrieval pipelines.
[06:29] Jordan: any other constraints?
[06:32] Marta: the main blockers are Samir's signoff on KMS and legal for DPA, then dev bandwidth. If Samir's comfortable we'll get the devs started.
[06:41] Samir: i'll need a doc listing encryption at rest, KMS flow, and audit export formats.
[06:47] Jordan: we'll send the security packet and a short KMS flow diagram. Also I will include a simple hosting comparison matrix (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with typical latency/cost brackets and time-to-first-token estimates.
[06:59] Evan: benchmark params — can you share the template?
[07:03] Priya: yes i'll share our perf template. It asks for: model, prompt distribution, avg tokens, concurrency, region, and auth method. We'll run a hosted run from eu-west and drop the results in the spreadsheet.
[07:15] Marta: about pricing — for Dedicated what's the commitment look like?
[07:20] Jordan: Dedicated is reserved capacity, monthly or annual commits. We can tailor a small starter pool for a 3-month pilot if you want to validate throughput before a larger commit.
[07:30] Samir: if we do private on-prem, how long to stand up?
[07:34] Priya: private on-prem varies — typical pilot is 4–8 weeks including network setup, KMS integration, and validation. VPC-hosted private control plane can be faster — 2–4 weeks.
[07:46] Evan: that's helpful. Any success stories in FS?
[07:49] Jordan: yes — a mid-market bank we worked with did self-serve pilot to prod in 6 weeks and then moved to Dedicated for cost predictability. They used our KV cache to cut token spend by ~30%.
[07:59] Marta: okay, i'm going to ask a practical question — can devs bypass SSO for quick experimentation with isolated accounts?
[08:06] Priya: yes — we can create developer API keys scoped to the quickstart org. We recommend short-lived keys for safety.
[08:13] Evan: for the PLG runway, what's the average conversion from free credits to a paid pilot?
[08:18] Jordan: it's variable, but a typical pattern is PLG pilot for 4–8 weeks, then a small Dedicated pilot or 3-month reserved for teams that need consistent latency and capacity. conversion depends on usage and compliance needs.
[08:31] Marta: let's talk specifics for next steps — can we get the security docs, credits, and a benchmark scheduled?
[08:36] Jordan: yes. I'll send the hosting matrix and pricing, attach the security packet, and provision 50k credits. Priya will share the benchmark template and coordinate a run.
[08:46] Samir: i'll provide KMS requirements and our DPA redlines.
[08:50] Jordan: perfect. we'll tentatively schedule the benchmark for next week. Priya, can you own scheduling?
[08:56] Priya: yep i'll reach out with times.
[09:00] Marta: thanks. One last thing — do you provide any managed ops for model rollouts? we want safe fallbacks if a model flop happens.
[09:08] Priya: yes — rollouts include canary, automated fallback to a lower-cost model, and routing by latency SLO. We can set automatic failover if error rates cross thresholds.
[09:19] Evan: awesome.
[09:22] Jordan: recap: Jordan send hosting matrix, pricing, security pack; grant 50k credits; Priya send perf template and schedule benchmark; Samir supply KMS and legal notes.
[09:33] Marta: cool, thanks everyone. we look forward to the quickstart.
[09:37] Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up in email with attachments and timeline.

(End of recorded transcript)
